WP2 · Work package

Prefix Constraint Compiler

Turns the policy into a short Constraint Summary Pack (CSP) for the VLA's prompt, so that the VLA knows the rules before it chooses an action. The goal is fewer rule-breaking commands, so the Shield has less to repair.

What the grant asks for

“Inject constraints — summarised, compressed, and risk-graded — into the VLA / planner input”Grant, Prefix Compiler page

Main files: guardrail/compiler.py guardrail/csp.py guardrail/paraphraser.py demo/real_vla_demo.py

Built

  • A typed Constraint Summary Pack

    The compiler turns the policy into a Constraint Summary Pack with the 14 fields the grant locks, described by a JSON Schema.

    guardrail/csp.py guardrail/csp.schema.json

  • Filtering, risk grading and a token budget

    Rules are filtered by mission area and time, graded by risk (0.5 severity + 0.3 proximity + 0.2 time-criticality) and fitted into a configurable budget of 256 tokens. P0 rules are always kept; if they alone exceed the budget, the compiler raises CSPBudgetExceeded instead of cutting silently.

    guardrail/csp.py

  • Readable rule sentences

    Each kept rule becomes a sentence from a Jinja2 template, with the reason it was kept. A time-windowed rule carries its window, and drops out of the pack outside it.

    guardrail/templates/

  • The pack reaches OpenVLA's prompt

    With --csp on, the real-VLA demo places the pack before OpenVLA's instruction and logs, for every inference, the exact prompt, its token count, and the pack and policy hashes. A prompt over budget is refused before the model loads.

    demo/real_vla_demo.py

  • A paraphraser

    112 free-form paraphrases (14 sets × 8) of task instructions and rule summaries for the VLA's prompt, generated once and stored with the prompt that produced them, a seeded template fallback, and a validator that compares each paraphrase's mission slots with the original.

    guardrail/paraphraser.py experiments/paraphrases/

Shown

  • Pack size on every project policy

    Across the 29 project policies the pack takes 54-106 OpenVLA tokens, inside the 256-token budget.

  • Covered by regression tests

    The pack, the OpenVLA prompt and the paraphraser each have their own regression test file, run with the project's full test suite.

    Reproduce: python tests/test_csp.py

Next for this work package

  • Next October – November 2026 Fly OpenVLA with the rule summary in its prompt, and compare missions with the summary on and off.
  • Next November 2026 Per-paraphrase robustness, measured with a pilot that reads text.
